What am I seeing?

Every point is a recorded neuron cell-body position. Brief orange and blue flashes show sharp rises and falls in its computed activity. Steady activity fades into the dim anatomical background.

These are change events derived from FLM’s continuous states, not biological action potentials. An event requires a change above 0.025 and 2.5 times that neuron’s recent average change, followed by a two-update cooldown. No random flashes or fixed number of active cells are added. The inspector shows the latest change (Δ).

The same full retained MaleCNS graph used by FLM: 166,700 neurons and 25,582,938 directed connections. Each update uses every connection, weighted by its share of the receiving neuron’s incoming synaptic contacts.

New bursts counts sharp activity changes in the latest step. Simulation steps counts completed whole-graph computations since reset. Last step time measures computation time, not conversation latency. The simulation stops and clears activity when the call ends.

This connectome is part of speech generation: its trained readout adjusts Moshi’s text predictions, which condition the audio model. Wiring and readout stay fixed during calls. This is an experimental integration, not evidence of better speech or biological fly language pathways. It does not model spikes or dopamine.
